data.command: What is Volt Typhoon's approach to critical infrastructure?

data.text:
So, you want to know about Volt Typhoon's approach to critical infrastructure? Well, let me tell you, we take it pretty seriously around here. We've got a centralized monitoring system set up using Prometheus and Grafana to keep an eye on all the important metrics. It's all fine-tuned to alert us if anything weird starts happening on the servers.

We're using a combination of Ansible and SaltStack for our configuration management, so everything's nice and consistent across the board. And, of course, we've got regular backups going on using Bacula - you know, just in case something goes south.

As for security, we're using a Linux-based system, so that's a good start, right? We've got fail2ban configured to block those pesky IP addresses that try to brute-force their way in, and we're running a couple of firewalls to keep the bad guys out. Oh, and let me tell you, our team is always on the lookout for any potential vulnerabilities and we patch things up ASAP.

But, I mean, critical infrastructure-wise, we've got a separate cluster for the databases, with a load balancer in front of it, and the web servers are all behind a HAProxy. It's all pretty standard
